mainTopic: Satan's lack of power on יום הכפורים, the times for תרומת הדשן, and רב's midnight division of the night, which רב כהנא challenges
overview: This amud finishes the אגדה in which אליהו explains to רב יהודה why people sin even on יום הכפורים: sin is always crouching at the door. רב יהודה then asks what השטן says about these sins. אליהו answers that השטן has no permission to accuse on יום הכפורים. רמי בר חמא proves this with גימטריא: השטן adds up to 364, so he has power on 364 days but not on the one remaining day. Next, a new משנה lists when the כהנים did תרומת הדשן. On a normal day it was done around the rooster's call, on יום הכפורים from midnight, and on the רגלים from the end of the first watch. The גמרא then quotes a משנה in זבחים: limbs that fall off the מזבח before midnight are put back, but after midnight they are treated as ashes. רב explains this midnight line by dividing the night, with the first half for burning and the second half for removing ashes. רב כהנא begins an objection from our משנה, since on the רגלים the ashes were removed before midnight; the challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Sin crouches at the door
steps.stepSummary: אליהו answers what הקב״ה says about people sinning even on יום הכפורים: the יצר הרע is always waiting at the door.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Sin lies in wait at the door."
steps.whatsHappening: This line continues a story from the previous page. אליהו quotes a פסוק to explain why people sin even on יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה had asked what הקב״ה says about sins committed on יום הכפורים. The answer quotes בראשית ד:ז: the יצר הרע is always crouching nearby, so it is no surprise that people sin. This sets up the next question about השטן.

phrases.english: "Sin lies in wait at the door."
phrases.notes: בראשית ד:ז. This is אליהו's answer from the end of the previous page.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives אליהו's answer to the question from the previous page. The dialogue then continues in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Sin is always waiting at the door, so people sin even on holy days.

steps.title: What does השטן say about it?
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה asks a follow-up question: what does השטן, the heavenly prosecutor, say about these sins?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה asks a follow-up question. If people sin on יום הכפורים, does השטן use it to accuse them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: השטן's job is to accuse people before הקב״ה. If sins happen on יום הכפורים, we would expect him to accuse. This question sets up the next answer.

phrases.english: And what did Satan say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up question to the answer in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether השטן accuses people for sins done on יום הכפורים.

steps.title: השטן has no permission to accuse on יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: אליהו answers that השטן has no permission to accuse on יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: השטן, on יום הכפורים, has no permission to accuse.
steps.whatsHappening: אליהו answers that השטן has no permission to accuse on יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sins can still happen on יום הכפורים, but השטן cannot use them as accusations on that day. The day is protected from his prosecution.

phrases.english: He said to him: Satan, on Yom Kippur,
has no permission to accuse.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: השטן has no authority to accuse on יום הכפורים.

steps.title: גימטריא proof that השטן rules only 364 days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source. רמי בר חמא shows that the letters of השטן add up to 364, meaning he has power on 364 days of the year but not on יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? רמי בר חמא said: The numerical value of "השטן" is 364. On 364 days he has permission to accuse. On יום הכפורים he has no permission to accuse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know that השטן is powerless on יום הכפורים. רמי בר חמא brings a proof from the numerical value (גימטריא) of the word השטן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters are ה=5, ש=300, ט=9, ן=50, which add up to 364. A solar year has 365 days, so one day is left over where השטן has no power. That day is יום הכפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: the numerical value of the letters in a word

steps.whatToRemember: השטן = 364 in גימטריא. He can accuse on 364 days of the year, but not on יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: From where do we know this? Rami bar Chama said:
"HaSatan" in numerical value
is three hundred sixty-four.
On three hundred sixty-four days
phrases.notes: Out of the 365 days of a solar year.

phrases.english: he has permission to accuse.
On Yom Kippur
he has no permission to accuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a source for the claim made in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That השטן cannot accuse on יום הכפורים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The גימטריא of the word השטן (364).

steps.title: Daily ash removal at the rooster's call
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה teaches that on a regular day, תרומת הדשן is done around the time of the rooster's call, slightly before or slightly after.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Every day they remove the ashes from the altar at the rooster's call or close to it, whether before it or after it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches when the כהנים did תרומת הדשן on a normal day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The time is not exact. It can be at the rooster's call or a little before or after. This normal-day rule is the baseline that the next lines will compare to.

keyTerms.meaning: they remove (the ashes), i.e., תרומת הדשן

steps.confusionAlert: תורמין את המזבח here does not mean separating תרומה from produce. It means removing a shovelful of ashes from the מזבח (תרומת הדשן).

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
Every day they remove the ashes from the altar
at the rooster's call or close to it,
whether before it or after it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה; it is unrelated to the אגדה before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ordinary days, תרומת הדשן is done around the rooster's call.

steps.title: Earlier times on יום הכפורים and the רגלים
steps.stepSummary: On יום הכפורים the ashes are removed from midnight. On the רגלים they are removed from the end of the first watch of the night.
steps.simpleTranslation: And on יום הכפורים, from midnight. And on the רגלים, from the first watch.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives earlier start times for special days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום הכפורים the כהן גדול has a heavy workload, so they start at midnight. On the רגלים there are many קרבנות, so they start even earlier, at the end of the first watch of the night.

keyTerms.meaning: the first watch of the night

phrases.english: and on Yom Kippur, from midnight,
and on the Festivals, from the first watch.
phrases.notes: That is, once the first watch of the night has ended.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds earlier exceptions to the normal-day timing in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום הכפורים, from midnight. On the רגלים, from the first watch.

steps.title: The courtyard was full before the rooster's call
steps.stepSummary: On the רגלים, the עזרה was already full of people before the rooster's call came.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the rooster's call would not arrive until the courtyard was full of Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes the scene on the רגלים. Crowds filled the עזרה very early, even before the rooster's call.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why the early start was needed. So many people came with קרבנות to offer that the work had to begin long before dawn.

phrases.english: And the rooster's call would not arrive
until the courtyard was full of Jews.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes the result of the early start on the רגלים in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the רגלים, the עזרה was full before the rooster's call.

steps.title: Limbs that fell off the altar: before or after midnight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from זבחים. Limbs that fall off the מזבח before midnight are put back and are subject to מעילה. After midnight they are not put back and there is no מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: We learned there: Limbs that burst off the altar, if before midnight, he returns them and one is liable for מעילה with them. If after midnight, he does not return them and one is not liable for מעילה with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related משנה from another מסכתא. It uses midnight as an important dividing line, which ties in with our משנה's יום הכפורים rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before midnight, the limbs still need to burn, so they are still holy. They are returned to the fire and carry מעילה. After midnight, the night's burning time is over, so they are treated like ashes: they are not returned and there is no מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: that burst off or sprang off (from the heat)
one is liable for מעילה (misusing הקדש)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
We learned there:
limbs that burst off the top of the altar,
before midnight, he returns them, and one is liable for misuse of them;

phrases.aramaic: לְאַחַר חֲצוֹת — לֹא יַחְזִיר, וְאֵין מוֹעֲלִין בָּהֶן.
phrases.english: after midnight, he does not return them, and one is not liable for misuse of them.
phrases.notes: They now have the status of ashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel משנה that also treats midnight as a key time, connecting to the יום הכפורים rule in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Midnight ends the limbs' burning period. After it, fallen limbs are treated as ashes.

steps.title: What is the source for the midnight line?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that midnight is the dividing line.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the midnight rule it just quoted. This sets up רב's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stated a rule with no פסוק. The גמרא wants to know what in the תורה tells us that midnight changes the limbs' status.

keyTerms.meaning: from where are these things derived?

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the midnight cutoff.

steps.title: רב divides the night in half
steps.stepSummary: רב notes that the פסוק links "all night" both to burning and to removing ashes. To resolve this, he splits the night: the first half for burning, the second half for removing ashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: One verse says, "All night... and he shall burn," and one verse says, "All night... and he shall remove." How can this be? Divide it: half of it for burning and half of it for removal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question. The פסוקים seem to give the whole night to two different jobs, so he divides the night between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק makes the whole night a time for burning the limbs. Another makes the whole night a time for removing ashes. Both cannot fill the entire night, so the first half goes to הקטרה and the second half to הרמה. That is why, after midnight, fallen limbs count as ashes.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, midnight splits the night. Before it, limbs are still being burned. After it, the time for removing ashes begins. This is why fallen limbs after midnight are treated as ashes. רב כהנא is about to challenge this division from our משנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: According to רב's division, the time for removing ashes should begin at midnight, which fits our משנה's יום הכפורים rule. But our משנה also allows removal on the רגלים from the end of the first watch, before midnight. רב כהנא raises exactly this problem in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav said: One verse says:
"All night... and he shall burn,"
and one verse says:
"All night... and he shall remove"
How can this be? Divide it:
half of it for burning, and half of it for removal.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two phrases each claim the whole night, so the night is split: the first half for burning, the second half for removing ashes.

steps.title: רב כהנא quotes a משנה about when ashes were removed
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא opens an objection to רב by quoting a משנה. It lists the times for removing the ashes: every day, on יום הכפורים, and on the רגלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא raised an objection: Every day they remove the ashes from the altar at the rooster's call, or close to it, either a little before or a little after. On יום הכפורים they start from midnight. On the רגלים they start from the end of the first watch of the night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. רב כהנא quotes a משנה about the times for removing the ashes. His actual question comes right on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב just said the second half of the night is for removing the ashes, so removal should not start before midnight. The משנה says that on the רגלים removal starts from the end of the first watch, which is earlier than midnight. That is the clash רב כהנא is about to point out.

keyTerms.meaning: Removing a portion of the ashes from the altar each morning (תרומת הדשן)
The first watch of the night, which ends before midnight

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the 'first watch' reaches midnight. The night has three or four watches, so the first watch ends before midnight. That early start time is the whole basis for the objection.
steps.whyThisMatters: If removing the ashes is set by the תורה for the second half of the night, an earlier start on the רגלים needs an explanation. The גמרא deals with this on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana raised an objection:
Every day they remove the ashes from the altar
phrases.notes: This is the start of the משנה being quoted.

phrases.english: at the rooster's call, or close to it,
whether a little before it or a little after it,
and on Yom Kippur, from midnight,
phrases.notes: This fits רב's rule of the second half of the night.

phrases.english: and on the Festivals, from the end of the first watch,
phrases.notes: This is earlier than midnight. It is the point that will clash with רב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This objects to רב's derivation in Step 10, which gave the second half of the night to removing the ashes.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that removing the ashes belongs to the second half of the night, starting at midnight.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה allows removal on the רגלים from the end of the first watch, which is before midnight. That contradicts the idea that the תורה sets midnight as the start of the time for removing the ashes.
